readings: Matching postseason batting records to players on `player_id`, work out each player's average postseason doubles per record (ignoring missing values), grouped by player and batting hand (`player.bats`). Turn that into a relative index by dividing it by the overall average of these per-player averages. Then compare each player's index with the average index of players who have the same batting hand. List the 10 players whose index is furthest above their batting-hand average. Show the player id, batting hand, average doubles, index, and index minus the hand average, sorted by that difference from highest to lowest (missing values last), unrounded. Leave out players whose batting hand is empty or missing (NULL) entirely, including from the overall average.
queries:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.player_id,
        p.bats,
        AVG(bp.double) AS average_doubles
    FROM player AS p
    JOIN batting_postseason AS bp ON bp.player_id = p.player_id
    WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL AND p.bats <> ''
    GROUP BY p.player_id, p.bats
),
player_indices AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        average_doubles,
        average_doubles / (SELECT AVG(average_doubles) FROM player_averages) AS idx
    FROM player_averages
),
hand_averages AS (
    SELECT bats, AVG(idx) AS hand_average_idx
    FROM player_indices
    GROUP BY bats
)
SELECT
    pi.player_id,
    pi.bats,
    pi.average_doubles,
    pi.idx,
    pi.idx - ha.hand_average_idx AS index_difference
FROM player_indices AS pi
JOIN hand_averages AS ha ON ha.bats = pi.bats
ORDER BY index_difference IS NULL, index_difference DESC
LIMIT 10;
